real_car: Triumph Spitfire Mk3/Mk4 1972 (soft top folded down)
body_style: 2-door convertible roadster, soft top folded down (open cockpit, windscreen only)

front.grille: low wide oval grille 13 units wide by 4 units high set in the nose front above the bumper at x 49, y 11..15, with one thin chrome bar and a small round badge at its centre
front.bumper: slim chrome blade across the nose 2.5 units high at y 8..10.5, x 46..50, with two small chrome over-riders
extras: headlamps sit in the front face of the one-piece bonnet, not in the wings

rear.taillamps: two small round lamps r 1.6 on the flat rear panel at x -49.5, y 13, set about 8 units either side of centre, with a small reversing lamp between them
rear.bumper: slim chrome blade across the tail 2.5 units high at y 8..10.5, x -50..-46, with two small over-riders
extras: flat near-vertical rear panel x -49.5..-50 from y 6.5 up to y 18.5
chrome boot lid handle on the rear deck at x -40, y 21.5
fuel filler cap on the rear left quarter at x -36, y 22

side_features: long one-piece front-hinged bonnet from the nose x 50 back to the scuttle x 8, its top edge a shallow crown falling from y 24.5 at the scuttle to y 19.5 at x 47
bonnet centre crease line running x 8..50 at y 19.5..24.5
cockpit opening lip (body top edge with the hood folded away) from the windscreen base x 8 back to the seat line x -14, at y 23.7..24.5
door panel gap line at x 5..8 from y 7 up to y 24
rounded front wheel arch centred x 28.2, radius 7.5
rounded rear wheel arch centred x -28.2, radius 7.5
straight sill line x -47..47 at y 6.5
chrome sill edge strip x -40..40 at y 6.5
special: hood folded DOWN: the cockpit is open behind the windscreen, so the windscreen top at y 30.5 is the highest point of the car
one-piece front-hinged bonnet covering the whole front half, front wings are part of it
long bonnet against a very short tail: the bonnet runs 42 units of the 100 unit length
twin round headlamps in bezels set into the front face of the bonnet
boot lid sits in the rear deck behind the cockpit lip, from x -16 back to x -46, with a chrome handle at its rear edge
the rear deck is level with the cockpit lip line, so there is no raised boot box; only a slight flare at the deck edges over the rear panel corners
notes: No web access, so dims_confidence is medium. Figures I am fairly sure of: length 3785 mm, wheelbase 2134 mm, tyre overall diameter about 570 mm (13 inch rims on 145 section tyres). Estimates I could not confirm: width 1450 mm (could be 1499 mm), height 1156 mm measured with the hood DOWN to the top of the windscreen, front and rear track 1230 mm each (the real front and rear tracks differ by only about 25 mm, so one figure is used for both), and the front/rear overhang split, which is drawn even at 28.2 units either side of centre; the real car's overhangs are close to equal so this is safe. The side outline is drawn from a written description of the car, not from a photo I could check: the long low bonnet crown falling from the scuttle (x 8.5, y 24.5) to the nose (x 47, y 19.5), the rounded nose dropping down the front face to a low grille, the windscreen raked back about 30 degrees from base y 24.4 to top y 30.5, the open cockpit lip running back nearly level to the seat line at x -14, then the rear deck falling gently to the flat near-vertical rear panel at x -49.2. Proportions that matter most: the 56.4 unit wheelbase (a long bonnet, short tail), the low 30.5 unit height, and the windscreen being the tallest point because the hood is down. ref_urls are the Wikipedia article and the Wikimedia Commons category, which I could not open to confirm they still exist.
